item.title: Watch Brewers fans celebrate 1st World Series game win in 44 years
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images Watch Brewers fans celebrate 1st World Series game win in 44 years appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After 44 long years of waiting, the Milwaukee Brewers have finally won a World Series game once again. The Brewers withstood a late Rays rally, one that included an overturned call on a potential game-ending double play, to claim the 3-2 win in Game 1. Following all the drama of the final inning, Brewers fans inside American Family Field let out a sigh of relief as they were finally able to celebrate the win after the final out. A fan video taken from the stands was able to see the ecstasy of the crowd as the Brewers clinched the victory. Brewers fans react to the franchise’s first World Series win in 44 years! pic.twitter.com/l32SUjiZat Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) October 24, 2026 Some Brewers fans may have thought they were in for a blowout win when Milwaukee got off to an early 2-0 lead in the first inning. Captain Christian Yelich drew first blood with an RBI triple off Nike Martinez. However, the Rays were able to recover after a rocky start and kept it close right until the end. Brewers closer Trevor Megill had some trouble closing the game out in the ninth. After a Yandy Diaz groundout, Megill surrendered back-to-back singles to Jonathan Aranda and Chandler Simpson. After a Rays double steal, the Brewers walked Junior Caminero to load the bases. Liam Hicks grounded out in the very next at-bat. While pinch runner Jorge Mateo scored, the Brewers thought they had turned the game-ending double play. But the Rays challenged and were able to get the call overturned. After the delay for the review, Megill was able to compose himself to strike out Jonny DeLuca to close out the game. Brewers fans will be hoping for another exciting game (and win) as Game 2 rolls along on Saturday night. Related: Brewers’ Aaron Ashby reveals how he found his postseason groove in 2026 Related: Brewers fans will love Christian Yelich’s locked in reaction to Game 1 win

item.title: Brewers fans will love Christian Yelich’s locked in reaction to Game 1 win
item.description: Credit: David Frerker-Imagn Images Brewers fans will love Christian Yelich’s locked in reaction to Game 1 win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers just won their first World Series game in 44 years, but Christian Yelich is not getting caught up in the moment. Yelich set the tone in Milwaukee’s 3-2 win over the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 1 on Friday night at American Family Field. Afterward, the longtime Brewers star made it clear the job is far from done. “Obviously happy that we won, but got to lock back in tomorrow,” Yelich said, via Pat Timlin of WISN 12 News. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Brewers won their first World Series game in 44 years, but Christian Yelich isn't celebrating anything yet. "Obviously happy that we won, but got to lock back in tomorrow" @Dario_Melendez | @WISN12News pic.twitter.com/EH5yaqewCv — Pat Timlin (@pat_timlin) October 24, 2026 It was a fitting message from one of the faces of the franchise. Yelich has been a cornerstone in Milwaukee since arriving in 2018, when he won National League MVP honors in his first season with the club. Now, he is finally getting his shot on the sport’s biggest stage. He wasted no time making an impact. With Jackson Chourio on base after a leadoff single in the first inning, Yelich lined a ball off Nick Martinez that sailed past center fielder Jonny DeLuca for an RBI triple . William Contreras followed with a single to bring Yelich home and give the Brewers a 2-0 lead. That early cushion proved important. Jacob Misiorowski held the Rays to one run over five innings , and his very first pitch of the World Series was clocked at 103.5 mph , a record for the Fall Classic. Tampa Bay had its chances, including a bases-loaded opportunity in the fifth, but could not break through. Chourio added an insurance run with an RBI single in the seventh. The ninth inning got tense. Trevor Megill loaded the bases, and what looked like a game-ending double play was overturned on replay, allowing the Rays to score. Megill recovered, though, striking out DeLuca to seal the win. The victory was Milwaukee’s first in the World Series since 1982, when the franchise fell to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games. The Brewers have never won a championship, and neither have the Rays . That history is exactly why Yelich wants his team to keep its focus. Game 2 is set for Saturday night in Milwaukee, where the Brewers will face Rays right-hander Drew Rasmussen with a chance to take a commanding lead before the series shifts to Tampa Bay. Related: Brewers’ Aaron Ashby reveals how he found his postseason groove in 2026 Related: Watch Brewers fans celebrate 1st World Series game win in 44 years

item.title: Brewers’ Pat Murphy gives ‘unbelievable’ praise to William Contreras after World Series Game 1
item.description: Kevin Sousa-Imagn Images Brewers’ Pat Murphy gives ‘unbelievable’ praise to William Contreras after World Series Game 1 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . For the first time in 44 years, the Milwaukee Brewers have won a World Series game. They took down the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday night to claim Game 1 of the 2026 World Series . William Contreras played a major role in this victory. Contreras had two hits on Friday night against Tampa Bay, while driving in a run. That run came in the first inning, but was big in the end. Milwaukee won by a narrow 3-2 scoreline to go up 1-0 in the 2026 World Series. After the game, the Brewers star received huge praise from manager Pat Murphy. “If anyone doesn’t notice the contributions of Contreras, he was the player of the game. He was unbelievable,” Murphy said, via local radio host Vincent Hesprich. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Scoring was not a common occurrence on Friday night. The Brewers scored twice in the opening inning to give themselves a 2-1 lead. The Rays would cut this in half when Liam Hicks drove in a run in the fourth inning. Jackson Chourio restored Milwaukee’s two-run lead in the seventh inning with a single. In the ninth inning, the Rays rallied and brought the game within a run again. However, it wasn’t enough, and Milwaukee defended home field for at least Game 1. This series is far from over, though. These are the two best teams in baseball fighting for the game’s ultimate prize. The Rays roll over, and the Brewers certainly want that 2-0 series lead heading into Tampa Bay. These teams retake the field on Saturday night for Game 2 at Miller Park in Milwaukee. Related: Brewers’ Aaron Ashby reveals how he found his postseason groove in 2026 Related: Watch Brewers fans celebrate 1st World Series game win in 44 years

item.title: Jack Crowell did it all as No. 1 New Canaan rallied past No. 2 Greenwich: Mike Anthony
item.description: New Canaan's Jackson Crowell (2) breaks through the line during the CIAC football game between the state's top two ranked teams, No. 1 New Canaan and No. 2 Greenwich high schools. Friday, October 23, 2026, Greenwich High School, Greenwich, Conn. (H John Voorhees III/Hearst Connecticut Media) GREENWICH - Even when Jack Crowell stands still, he seems to be doing a little bit of everything. As a linebacker, he hovers just beyond scrimmage, head on a swivel. He analyzes, points, screams, adding elements of raw emotion and astute organization to the New Canaan football team's defense. He stands out immediately in the middle of the field. And the longer you watch, he stands out all over. He's on both sides of the ball. He stretches the field. On Friday, he was even turning the corner for a fourth-quarter touchdown that basically sealed the top-ranked Rams' 23-19 victory over No. 2 Greenwich Friday night in a high school football game that the entire state had its eyes on. "I was trying to look for the edge," Crowell said of his run right, which came on 4 th and goal from the 4 and gave New Canaan a 10-point lead with 7:39 to play. "I didn't know for sure that I was going to have it. I was kind of looking to cut up one of the blockers. But when I saw the end zone, I mean, green grass. So it was pretty exciting." Crowell was back on the field for the first play following the kickoff. He thwarted Greenwich quarterback Phil Tarantino's rushing attempt with a vicious hit for a 2-yard loss, the back end of a sequence that said so much about this game. Crowell was the best player on the field. And New Canaan was the best team on the field in a matchup between the top two teams in the GametimeCT Top 10 Poll . It's too bad the FCIAC doesn't have a conference championship anymore because football doesn't get better than this, even in state tournaments. This was hardly a season-defining victory for New Canaan (Class L) or a season-defining loss for Greenwich (Class LL). Both could go on and win state championships in their respective classes again. But it sure was something to see, with two of Connecticut's best teams lining up to measure up. The best players tend to rise to the occasion during such experiences. "Pre-game, I was jumping around," Crowell said. "Maybe I jumped around too much because I was cramping in the game. But I was just really excited. They just debuted their black jerseys, which was pretty cool. And with Youth Night - and I think they inducted people into their hall of fame - it was just an important night and it's awesome that we were able to be a part of it, and even more awesome that we came away with the win." Crowell, named the 2026 boys athlete of the year at the GametimeCT High School Sports Awards Show in June , is a three-sport star. He is a standout defenseman for New Canaan in hockey and arguably the state's best goalie in lacrosse, the sport he has chosen to play next year at Princeton. Obviously, he's a hell of a football player
item.content:encoded: New Canaan's Jackson Crowell (2) breaks through the line during the CIAC football game between the state's top two ranked teams, No. 1 New Canaan and No. 2 Greenwich high schools. Friday, October 23, 2026, Greenwich High School, Greenwich, Conn. (H John Voorhees III/Hearst Connecticut Media) GREENWICH - Even when Jack Crowell stands still, he seems to be doing a little bit of everything. As a linebacker, he hovers just beyond scrimmage, head on a swivel. He analyzes, points, screams, adding elements of raw emotion and astute organization to the New Canaan football team's defense. He stands out immediately in the middle of the field. And the longer you watch, he stands out all over. He's on both sides of the ball. He stretches the field. On Friday, he was even turning the corner for a fourth-quarter touchdown that basically sealed the top-ranked Rams' 23-19 victory over No. 2 Greenwich Friday night in a high school football game that the entire state had its eyes on. "I was trying to look for the edge," Crowell said of his run right, which came on 4 th and goal from the 4 and gave New Canaan a 10-point lead with 7:39 to play. "I didn't know for sure that I was going to have it. I was kind of looking to cut up one of the blockers. But when I saw the end zone, I mean, green grass. So it was pretty exciting." Crowell was back on the field for the first play following the kickoff. He thwarted Greenwich quarterback Phil Tarantino's rushing attempt with a vicious hit for a 2-yard loss, the back end of a sequence that said so much about this game. Crowell was the best player on the field. And New Canaan was the best team on the field in a matchup between the top two teams in the GametimeCT Top 10 Poll . It's too bad the FCIAC doesn't have a conference championship anymore because football doesn't get better than this, even in state tournaments. This was hardly a season-defining victory for New Canaan (Class L) or a season-defining loss for Greenwich (Class LL). Both could go on and win state championships in their respective classes again. But it sure was something to see, with two of Connecticut's best teams lining up to measure up. The best players tend to rise to the occasion during such experiences. "Pre-game, I was jumping around," Crowell said. "Maybe I jumped around too much because I was cramping in the game. But I was just really excited. They just debuted their black jerseys, which was pretty cool. And with Youth Night - and I think they inducted people into their hall of fame - it was just an important night and it's awesome that we were able to be a part of it, and even more awesome that we came away with the win." Crowell, named the 2026 boys athlete of the year at the GametimeCT High School Sports Awards Show in June , is a three-sport star. He is a standout defenseman for New Canaan in hockey and arguably the state's best goalie in lacrosse, the sport he has chosen to play next year at Princeton. Obviously, he's a hell of a football player, too. Crowell had two touchdown rushes on Friday night, setting up the first one with his own interception and a 47-yard return to the 2. "A little sad I didn't get in t0he end zone," Crowell said. "But …" Coach Lou Marinelli figured it was only right to hand Crowell the ball from there. Crowell's first rushing touchdown opened the scoring, another stamp on a game he dominated. "He loves football," Marinelli said. "He absolutely loves football. I think he wishes he was 6-3 and 250 and playing at Alabama. He's just a great captain. I can't say enough good things about him. Whoever does Gatorade player of the year should really consider him for all he does. He plays offense. He plays defense. He's our captain. He's a great player. Just a really heads-up kid. I'm glad he's playing for us." Crowell (5-9, 185) had just three carries in New Canaan's first five games, for 53 yards and a touchdown. He carried 10 times 35 yards and two touchdowns on Friday, when the bleachers were packed, maybe a couple thousand fans. It was electric at Cardinal Stadium. New Canaan trailed 13-9 at halftime but went big, and to the ground attack, to push its winning streak to increasingly remarkable territory. Finn Mocco, Dallas George, Ben Scott and Crowell pulled the offense along with the game on the line. "We have all these big guys in front of us," Crowell said. "It kind of makes our life easy. I'm kind of just picking these gaps, 4- and 5-yard gains. If you get that every play, it's really what you're looking for. It is a great feeling to beat them here." Both teams entered 5-0. New Canaan won last year's matchup, too, and both went on to win state championships. New Canaan has won four titles in a row, Greenwich two in a row. If Connecticut has a legitimate claim to showcase good high school football, this was the game to display. New Canaan has won 29 games in a row, last losing in 2024, Crowell's sophomore year. After the latest victory, the team took a knee in front of Marinelli and one player shouted, "Doesn't get any easier from here!" That's right. The FCIAC is a beast. There's a lot of season ahead. "Isn't that the greatest thing, though? Isn't that why you play?" Marinelli said. "You want to play in games like this. You want to be able to compete. That was the first time our kids got really punched in the mouth and had to fight their way back. We learned a lot of lessons today. And, all good." Members of the St. Joe's team, tied with Greenwich for No. 2 in the GameTimeCT poll, were in attendance. New Canaan plays No. 6 Ludlowe next week, then St. Joseph. Greenwich plays Ridgefield next, followed by Wilton, St. Joseph and Staples. It's a long season. Friday was a fun night. "First time we were really in a game," Marinelli said. "To come from behind like that, I think was important." Crowell acknowledged that he is cherishing opportunities like Friday's more so than ever. He has just four regular-season games remaining in his football career, plus playoff games. He'll be at hockey rinks soon enough, then on the lacrosse field, and at Princeton before we know it. When Crowell looks back on his high school football experience, surely part of his mind will focus on that Friday night October game that all of Connecticut was watching. "One versus two for a reason," Crowell said. "The atmosphere was awesome. It's easy to get hyped for these games. It was easy to rally the guys." Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. Get the biggest headlines of the day from our network of journalists around the state. item.title: Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski drops brutally honest admission on his Game 1 start
item.description: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski drops brutally honest admission on his Game 1 start appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers possessed a top-notch bullpen in the regular season and in the last two rounds of the playoffs, but the idea of this team winning a championship without Jacob Misiorowski posting his best stuff seemed near-incomprehensible. The presumptive National League Cy Young was unable to reach the sixth inning for a third straight postseason start, and yet, the Brew Crew are now just three wins away from capturing their first World Series title in franchise history. Misiorowski pitched five innings of one-run ball in Friday’s 3-2 Game 1 victory versus the Tampa Bay Rays, allowing four hits while recording three strikeouts and one walk. He perfectly described his fairly short yet triumphant outing. “Not perfect, good enough to get a win,” the genial 24-year-old right-hander said, via Joey Mistretta of ClutchPoints. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Misiorowski has not been operating as a work horse for some time. He has accumulated only a combined 13 1/3 innings of work across three playoff outings. The three Ks are also surprisingly low . This record-breaking flamethrower is nearing the end of his first full MLB campaign, and he is showing the effects of unleashing elite velocity all yearlong. Like Misiorowski said, though, he had enough on this night. The Brewers’ bullpen also provided first-class reinforcements, once again. Aaron Ashby remains unstoppable, Abner Uribe enjoyed a stellar showing in his own right and Trevor Megill survived despite allowing one run in the ninth. The lineup notched timely hits, as it does, and All-Star catcher William Contreras threw out potential game-tying runs multiple times. Jacob Misiorowski did not carry the squad to a 1-0 series lead in American Family Field. Pat Murphy has not asked him to fill that role during this postseason. Milwaukee secured the W by putting forth a complete effort. This ballclub may not have many household names, but it should be obvious by now that one player does not define Brewers baseball. If Milwaukee has its way, Misiorowski will not have to put the team on his back again for the rest of 2026. Game 2 is Saturday at approximately 8 p.m. ET. Related: Brewers’ Aaron Ashby reveals how he found his postseason groove in 2026 Related: Watch Brewers fans celebrate 1st World Series game win in 44 years

item.title: Michael Carrick and Man United go in search for big win against bogey side who have made their life a living hell recently
item.description: Michael Carrick and Man United go in search for big win against bogey side who have made their life a living hell recently Manchester United will take on AFC Bournemouth on Sunday afternoon after a seven-match winless run. The Red Devils have not registered a victory in the Premier League in almost two months, since defeating Ipswich Town at the end of August. United have played the Cherries 26 times , winning 14. Bournemouth have come out on top five times, with there being seven draws. Here are three storylines to get the blood racing. Poor recent record Unfortunately, United are developing the habit of collecting bogey sides, but few are worse than Bournemouth as of late. Whilst Michael Carrick’s side dominate the historical record, it is the side from the south coast that have had the most to smile about in recent years. United have not beaten Bournemouth in their last six encounters, with there being four draws and two losses. The two defeats have also, worryingly, been 0-3 defeats at Old Trafford, an unthinkable result for United on Sunday in this current context. In fact, the last win for United was a 0-1 victory at the Vitality Stadium in 2023. Goals galore This fixture is also usually entertaining in terms of goals. Last season saw a rollercoaster 4-4 draw between the two sides, and the match also finished 2-2 on the south coast. In fact, there has never been a goalless draw between the two sides in all 26 encounters. There have also been a total of 21 goals in the last five matches between the two teams. Bruno Fernandes and Marcus Rashford joy It is safe to say that neither player is in their best moment. Fernandes has struggled for form and has been involved in controversy off the pitch after his recent outburst against the coaches’ tactics following the 1-4 defeat to 1907 Como. Rashford has also found himself left out of the starting line-up and having little effect on proceedings lately. Nonetheless, both have good records versus the Cherries. Fernandes has nine goals and assists in nine appearances, whilst Marcus Rashford has six in seven matches against them. Man United results vs Bournemouth Page 1 of 2 1 2

Rashford has also found himself left out of the starting line-up and having little effect on proceedings lately. Nonetheless, both have good records versus the Cherries. Fernandes has nine goals and assists in nine appearances, whilst Marcus Rashford has six in seven matches against them. Man United results vs Bournemouth Page 1 of 2 1 2

"I love that my coach believes in me and, I don't know..." Webb said. "He's a really reliable teammate. He'll do anything for the team. He well. He will put his body on the line," Testerman interjected. Ever since Wynn got to Independence, the Pioneers have broken every huddle, every weight session, every film study with two words: Beat Ryle. The win, coupled with Campbell County's win at Great Crossing, made for an extra sweet Friday night at Chlorine Menefee Stadium. "This win means everything. It's been years since we won a district championship, and being able to do it, it really brings back the tradition and celebration of our program," Webb said. Here's a rundown of all the district champions in Northern Kentucky: Class 1A, District 3: After starting the regular season 1-5 and nearly dropping their first district game to rival Newport, the Newport Central Catholic Thoroughbreds are on a three-game winning streak and have yet again won their district. A 47-7 win over previously undefeated Dayton boosted morale and they ran away from Bellevue in the second half. NewCath will host Trimble County on Nov. 6. Class 1A, District 4: After a two-game losing streak in the middle of the season, the Holy Cross Indians dominated in wins over Bishop Brossart, Trimble County and Ludlow to earn two home playoff games. The first of those will come against Bellevue on Nov. 6, one week after the Indians host the Tigers to close out the regular season. Class 2A, District 5: Beechwood outscored its district opponents 320-7 this season. That's kind of what the Tigers do every year. After facing Campbell County to close the regular season, they'll open the playoffs against Morgan County. Thanks to a 35-0 win over St. Henry, Walton-Verona earned the No. 2 seed and will host Jackson County. St. Henry is the 3-seed, but could also win a playoff game; the Crusaders will travel to West Carter. Class 3A, District 5: The top seed in this district came down to a controversial call at the end of Lloyd Memorial's game at Bourbon County, a game the Colonels ended up winning. Still, Lloyd will get a home playoff game, hosting East Carter on Nov. 6. Class 4A, District 5: The Highlands Bluebirds have looked the part of a state championship contender since a 41-21 win over Boyle County. They allowed just 26 points in district play and finished the season with a win over Scott County that should really help their RPI for the postseason. Class 5A, District 5: The Cooper Jaguars got their district schedule off to a shaky start with a 22-21 win over Conner, but won their other three games by double-digit points. That's three straight district titles for Cooper, which will host Anderson County to start the playoffs. Deer Park beats Wyoming, causes three-way CHL tie A win for Wyoming was all the Cowboys needed for another solo Cincinnati Hills League crown. Instead, Deer Park beat Wyoming 41-21, giving those two and Indian Hill a three-way tie for the league championship. Wyoming had defeated Indian Hill 48-47 in triple overtime on Sept. 11 and Indian Hill beat Deer Park 42-22 on Oct. 16. Deer Park’s victory was its first over Wyoming since 2006 and it was Wyoming’s first regular season league loss to a team other than Indian Hill since 2015. The result? Deer Park’s first ever CHL championship and the league’s first three-way tie since Indian Hill, Wyoming and Madeira shared it in 1999. McNicholas beats Badin and wins first conference crown since 2017 Badin has won or shared a Greater Catholic League title each season since 2018. The last time the Rams didn’t grab a share? That was in 2017 when McNicholas won the GCL-Coed’s Central division. Well, the last time until McNicholas beat Badin 14-0 on Oct. 23, giving McNicholas the solo conference title with a 5-0 mark in the league. Badin and Alter tied for second with 3-2 records. Max Orlando had a receiving touchdown and recovered a fumble at his team’s own one-yard line in the second quarter. Joe Reuss added another before halftime and the 14-0 lead was all the Rockets needed for the win. Top individual performers in Week 10 Bryce Armstrong, Highlands: The sophomore quarterback soared in a 34-13 win against Class 5A No. 2 Scott County, throwing and running for a combined 333 yards and two touchdowns. Lucas Cannady, St. Bernard-Elmwood Place: The senior signal caller was 8-for-10 for 252 yards and six touchdowns and an interception in the 41-0 win against Stivers. Drew Dailey, Lakota East: The sophomore, in a 45-13 win against Sycamore, had eight carries for 157 yards and two touchdowns. Devlan Daniel, Indian Hill: In a 38-0 win at Reading that helped Indian Hill clinch a share of the CHL title, Daniel was 4-of-7 for 68 yards and two touchdowns in the air while notching five carries for 120 yards and another touchdown. Kaden Estep, Elder: In a 52-6 win against Maryland's Mount Zion Prep, Estep was 11-of-14 for 220 yards and five touchdowns. In the game, he broke Elder's career passing yardage record previously held by Peyton Ramsey. Anquan Evans, Oak Hills: Despite a 42-14 loss to Lakota West, Evans had 23 carries for 157 yards and both touchdowns for the Highlanders. Ben Frye, Turpin: The senior had a pair of interceptions as Turpin beat Milford 49-12, giving him four for the campaign. Carter Jones, Lakota East: In a 45-13 win over Sycamore, Jones had seven receptions for 110 yards and two scores. Brady Lawhon, Harrison: The senior quarterback accounted for five touchdowns in a 41-13 win against Northwest to claim the final SWOC championship. Kolby Morgerson, Middletown: In his second game back after a three-week layoff, Morgerson led Middletown to a 63-6 win at Hamilton. He was 10-of-14 passing for 177 yards and two touchdowns. Caleyn Murray, Walnut Hills: The senior capped his career with four receptions, 153 yards and two touchdowns in a 56-14 loss to Kings. Alex Nagel, Mason: Nagel was 4-for-6 passing for 138 yards while carrying the ball 35 times for 234 yards and three touchdowns as Mason beat Colerain 42-33. Kenyon Norman, Lakota West: The senior back had 126 yards and four touchdowns on 14 carries in a 42-14 win at Oak Hills, giving him 1,616 yards and 32 touchdowns for the season. item.title: Bryan Jasso's late field goal sends Brackenridge over Jefferson into playoffs
item.description: After Brackenridge receiver Damien Castro Diaz's (4) reception tied the score he was mobbed by teammates in the second half of a District 14-5A-II football game Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026 at San Antonio ISD Sports Complex. Brackenridge rallied from behind to beat Jefferson on a late field goal Friday and clinch the program's first playoff spot since 2021. (Ronald Cortes/for the San Antonio Express News) With Brackenridge trailing Jefferson by 1 with under two minutes left, Eagles coach Steve Garcia had one question for his team. "How bad do you want it?" The Eagles offense answered the call by driving 22 yards in six plays before sophomore Bryan Jasso kicked the go-ahead, 29-yard field goal, securing a 23-21 win over Jefferson on Friday at SAISD Sports Complex. In 2023 and 2024, the Eagles were winless. Now, for the first time under Garcia, they're heading to the playoffs. The accomplishment drove him to tears. "When I took this job, we were 0-20," Garcia said. "There were a lot of naysayers. Being an SAISD product, I knew Brackenridge was going to be back. We're not officially back just yet, but we're almost there." Brackenridge leaned on senior Cruz Castillo to kickstart its offense early. Castillo churned out 34 rushing yards on the Eagles' opening drive before sophomore Joshua Garcia flipped the script and launched a 31-yard touchdown pass to senior Jarred Jones. Jefferson tried a similar approach on its first drive, riding senior Michael Bejar for 29 yards, but the Mustangs turned the ball over on downs in Eagles territory. The Mustangs snatched possession back after senior John Fernandez nabbed a tip-drill interception on Joshua Garcia. Senior Daniel Rincon returned the favor on Jefferson's ensuing drive, picking off Mustangs senior Noah Hernandez after Hernandez overshot his target. Brackenridge squandered Rincon's big play, but Rincon gave his team another shot. Battling through an offensive pass interference, Rincon hauled in his second interception. "Hard work pays off," Rincon said. After a 1-yard loss from Castillo, Steve Garcia rewarded Rincon by drawing up a play for him. On second-and-11, Joshua Garcia hit Rincon on a quick slant, and Rincon did the rest, shaking a tackler and outrunning defenders for a 71-yard score to put the Eagles up 14-0 with 6:12 left in the half. "Daniel stepped up today," Steve Garcia said. "He earned that. He earned his wings tonight." With 12 seconds left in the half, Hernandez found sophomore Randy Badillo Jr. for a 12-yard touchdown. A successful 2-point try made it a one-possession game at halftime. Jefferson took its first lead of the game late in the third quarter after Bejar connected with senior John Fernandez for a 19-yard double-pass touchdown. Now trailing 15-14, Brackenridge settled in and continued pounding the rock with Castillo. The Eagles rushed eight times to get Jefferson keyed in on the run. The plan worked, and Joshua Garcia took a low snap to bait Jefferson before finding Rincon for a 27-yard score. A missed extra point left the Eagles leading 20-15 with 10:19 remaining in the game. A quick turnover-on-downs seemed like the end for the Mustangs, but a missed 39-yarder from Jasso gave them life late. Bejar capitalized on Jefferson's second play after the missed field goal, breaking loose for a 73-yard touchdown. Brackenridge began its final drive in plus territory after a pivotal kick return. Despite starting at the Jefferson 32-yard line, the Eagles were still forced into a fourth-and-10 situation. With the game on the line, Brackenridge went to Rincon to get the first down, and he converted. Even after Jasso's earlier miss, Steve Garcia wanted to give him another shot to win the game. This time, Jasso delivered and secured his team's first playoff bid since 2021. "These games are won in the offseason," Steve Garcia said. "Our guys bought in. I told the guys, ‘Just believe in us, believe in yourself. We're good. We're a playoff team.' And they showed that tonight." Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. item.title: Lakeland Christian makes statement with dominating win over Victory
item.description: LAKELAND — Lakeland Christian didn’t fool around with so much on the line. The Vikings took control of the game early and never let their foot off the gas en route to a 41-7 victory over Victory Christian on Friday night in the showdown between Class 1A, District 7 rivals at Southeastern’s Victory Field. LCS (8-0-1, 4-0) not only clinched the district title, its third district title for football in school history, it avenged last season’s playoff loss to Victory Christian (6-3, 3-1). It was a dominant performance as Lakeland Christian finished with 358 yards of total offense while holding Victory to just 124 yards, including less than 100 yards until the final minutes of the game. The Vikings also came up with three interceptions. “The defense played great,” LCS coach Danny Williams said. “We took away some things that they wanted to do and made them do some things they probably weren't comfortable with.” Here are three takeaways from the Vikings’ victory. LCS strikes fast Lakeland Christian made a statement when it drove 82 yards on just six plays on its first drive of the game game, taking a 7-0 lead on Brady Brenneman’s 44-yard touchdown pass to Messiah Borders. The Vikings’ defense stiffened to stop Victory on fourth down on the following drive. LCS then went 66 yards on 12 plays to take a 14-0 lead with seven seconds left to play on Brenneman’s 6-yard pass to Jack Jenkins. “We, haven’t been able to jump out on them in every game we played,” LCS coach Danny Williams. “So that was good.” By halftime, it was 28-0 as AJ Truedell, who rushed for 106 yards on 16 carries, scored twice on runs of 27 yards and 8 yards. LCS wins QB battle There’s no doubt that Victory Christian eighth-grade QB Jaxon Smith has tremendous upside, but this night belonged to Brenneman. The USF-bound senior completed 18 of 24 passes for 229 yards and two touchdowns. Smith was just 6 of 16 for 48 hours, but he wasn’t helped out y his teammates, who can up with several Vikings show off their WR depth Lakeland Christian was already down two wide receiver in Cael Straub and Markus Bangston who were out with injuries. The Vikings then lost Borders late in the second quarter when he was ejected. Borders, who caught three passes for 53 yards will miss at least next week’s regular-season finale. Brenneman, however, spread the ball around as he completed passes to at least seven different players. Sophomore Jayden Wall led with five receptions for 77 yards. Straub and Langston both could be back for the first week of the playoffs. This article originally appeared on The Ledger: Lakeland Christian makes statement with dominating win over Victory

item.title: Knicks make unfortunate NBA Champion history not seen since 2012
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Knicks make unfortunate NBA Champion history not seen since 2012 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Knicks ’ title defense is off to a rocky start, and the slow beginning has put them in some unwanted company. After falling 107-103 to the Boston Celtics on Friday night at TD Garden , the Knicks are 0-2. That makes them the first reigning NBA champion to drop its first two games of a season since the 2011-12 Dallas Mavericks, who went on to lose their first three. Since then, every reigning champion had won at least one of its first two games, a stretch that included the 2015-16 Golden State Warriors opening 24-0. It is a jarring turn for a franchise that was celebrating just days ago. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) New York raised its first championship banner in 53 years on Tuesday at Madison Square Garden after beating the San Antonio Spurs 4-1 in the NBA Finals. The party was short-lived, as the Philadelphia 76ers spoiled ring night with a 106-100 win behind 28 points from Tyrese Maxey and the regular-season debuts of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. Friday’s loss followed a similar script. The Knicks hung around all night and had chances late, but they could not close. New York used a 12-3 run to cut a 12-point deficit to three, and Jalen Brunson later trimmed it to 99-98 with 1:41 remaining. Jayson Tatum took over from there. The Celtics star scored seven of Boston’s final eight points , including a three-pointer in the final minute that sealed it, and finished with a game-high 36. Karl-Anthony Towns led New York with 22 points, while OG Anunoby added 20 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. Deuce McBride chipped in 20 off the bench, and Brunson scored 19. Brunson has not looked like himself through two games. He shot just 6-of-19 against Philadelphia and was held to 19 points in Boston. New York is also adjusting to life without Mitchell Robinson , the lone member of its championship rotation who did not return, after he signed with Boston. There is still no reason to panic in late October. Those 2011-12 Mavericks were also coming off a title, and while their championship defense ended in a first-round sweep, two games hardly define a season. Still, the Knicks will want to stop the skid quickly before it becomes a bigger storyline. They return home to host the Orlando Magic on Sunday, looking for their first win as defending champions. Related: Knicks’ Karl-Anthony Towns, Mitchell Robinson share special moments after Celtics take down NY Related: Knicks’ Karl-Anthony Towns finds himself on the wrong side of a Mitchell Robinson block

item.title: UConn tops UMass, 35-16
item.description: Sep 5, 2026; East Hartford, Connecticut, USA; UConn Huskies quarterback Kalieb Osborne (7) throws a pass against the Lafayette Leopards in the second quarter at Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The UConn Huskies (4-3) defeated the UMass Minutemen (4-4), 35-16, to win their fourth straight over the Minutemen. Quarterback Kalieb Osborne completed 14 of 19 (73.7%) passes for 173 yards and two touchdowns. Cyncir Bowers led the way on the ground with 132 rushing yards, while Osborne added 81 yards and both scored a touchdown. JD Willoughby tallied 65 yards and a touchdown to lead the Husky receivers. Defensively, the Huskies held UMass to just 53 rushing yards. The visitors came into the game averaging 160.1 rushing yards per contest. The defense notched a pair of sacks but no turnovers, holding the Minutemen scoreless for nine straight possessions after allowing a field goal on the opening drive. “We really challenged them to throw the ball,” head coach Jason Candle said. “When you’re able to compress the pocket and do a good job not allowing an athletic quarterback to escape to his dominant hand, it really takes an unselfish approach by the defensive front.” UMass QB William “Pop” Watson III started his first game after missing the last two, completing 22 of 38 (57.9%) passes for 205 yards and a touchdown that came when the score was 28-3 in the third quarter. On that first drive, Watson nailed wide-open wideout Drew Alsup down the middle for 23 yards. A trick-play pass to Watson got them to the 18-yard line before a pass to tight end Max Dowling at the 5-yard line. UConn’s defense held at the goal-line to keep them out of the end zone. Connecticut began its first drive with a false start. However, Ky Wilson drew a pass interference that got them to midfield. Then, Shamar Porter caught an 11-yard pass and Bowers hurdled over a defender to get to the 38-yard marker. Osborne connected with Porter again for a 5-yard touchdown to get it to 7-3 at the end of the first quarter. In the second quarter, seven consecutive three-and-outs occurred across both teams. Until the two-minute warning, the Huskies entered enemy territory once. They got good field position after a punt, on their own 45. After some Bowers runs got them to the 20-yard line, Osborne threw an over-the-shoulder pass to Willoughby for a touchdown, making it 14-3. With a minute and a half before halftime, the defense forced another three-and-out, getting the ball back with a little over a minute left. On the first play, Bowers rushed up the middle, danced around some defenders, and then bolted for a 70-yard house call. At 7-3 before the two-minute timeout, the score was 21-3 at halftime after Bowers’ second 70-plus-yard TD of the year. item.content:encoded: Sep 5, 2026; East Hartford, Connecticut, USA; UConn Huskies quarterback Kalieb Osborne (7) throws a pass against the Lafayette Leopards in the second quarter at Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The UConn Huskies (4-3) defeated the UMass Minutemen (4-4), 35-16, to win their fourth straight over the Minutemen. Quarterback Kalieb Osborne completed 14 of 19 (73.7%) passes for 173 yards and two touchdowns. Cyncir Bowers led the way on the ground with 132 rushing yards, while Osborne added 81 yards and both scored a touchdown. JD Willoughby tallied 65 yards and a touchdown to lead the Husky receivers. Defensively, the Huskies held UMass to just 53 rushing yards. The visitors came into the game averaging 160.1 rushing yards per contest. The defense notched a pair of sacks but no turnovers, holding the Minutemen scoreless for nine straight possessions after allowing a field goal on the opening drive. “We really challenged them to throw the ball,” head coach Jason Candle said. “When you’re able to compress the pocket and do a good job not allowing an athletic quarterback to escape to his dominant hand, it really takes an unselfish approach by the defensive front.” UMass QB William “Pop” Watson III started his first game after missing the last two, completing 22 of 38 (57.9%) passes for 205 yards and a touchdown that came when the score was 28-3 in the third quarter. On that first drive, Watson nailed wide-open wideout Drew Alsup down the middle for 23 yards. A trick-play pass to Watson got them to the 18-yard line before a pass to tight end Max Dowling at the 5-yard line. UConn’s defense held at the goal-line to keep them out of the end zone. Connecticut began its first drive with a false start. However, Ky Wilson drew a pass interference that got them to midfield. Then, Shamar Porter caught an 11-yard pass and Bowers hurdled over a defender to get to the 38-yard marker. Osborne connected with Porter again for a 5-yard touchdown to get it to 7-3 at the end of the first quarter. In the second quarter, seven consecutive three-and-outs occurred across both teams. Until the two-minute warning, the Huskies entered enemy territory once. They got good field position after a punt, on their own 45. After some Bowers runs got them to the 20-yard line, Osborne threw an over-the-shoulder pass to Willoughby for a touchdown, making it 14-3. With a minute and a half before halftime, the defense forced another three-and-out, getting the ball back with a little over a minute left. On the first play, Bowers rushed up the middle, danced around some defenders, and then bolted for a 70-yard house call. At 7-3 before the two-minute timeout, the score was 21-3 at halftime after Bowers’ second 70-plus-yard TD of the year. On UMass’ second offensive possession in the third quarter, Porter blocked Edward Phillipson’s punt and recovered it in the endzone. Midway through the third quarter, UConn led 28-3. The Huskies’ last blocked punt for a touchdown was in 2012 against UMass. “I always saw a willing blocker and a guy that was able to make contested catches,” Candle said of Porter. “With Javon [Brown] out, he’s had to step up and has continued doing a really good job being the main X receiver.” With five and a half minutes remaining in the third period, from the 24-yard line, Jack O’Connor missed the field goal. The Minutemen took over and receiver Joseph Griffin Jr. reeled in a 41-yard pass down the sideline. Watson finished the drive with a touchdown pass to Curtis Kimmons IV to make it 28-9 after a missed conversion. Osborne’s rushing TD capped off a drive where the Huskies were getting yards in chunks, making it 35-9 before another garbage time TD from the minutemen got us to the final score. Next up, the Huskies travel to face the Air Force Falcons on Saturday, Oct. 31 at 3 p.m. The game will be televised on Mountain West Plus.

item.title: PREVIEW: Stamford Bridge awaits as Chelsea and Spurs renew rivalry
item.description: PREVIEW: Stamford Bridge awaits as Chelsea and Spurs renew rivalry Chelsea host Tottenham on Saturday, with the Blues sitting fourth in the table while 16th-placed Spurs arrive fresh from their first league win of the season. The west London side have bounced back from a three-match winless run with back-to-back victories. They thrashed Bournemouth 5-1 at home before following it up with a 2-0 away win over Everton. Alonso’s squad remains unbeaten at home in the top flight this season. Pedro Neto bagged a brace in Chelsea’s latest game against the Toffees on 17 October. His opener came just 43 seconds into the second half before he doubled his tally in the 90th minute. The result marked the Blues’ first Premier League clean sheet this season. João Pedro is Chelsea’s leading scorer with five goals, putting him joint-second in the Premier League scoring charts so far this term. The Brazilian has also registered three assists. Tottenham entered Monday night’s match against Coventry without a win in their opening six fixtures. Three draws and three defeats had left Spurs bottom of the table before they beat Coventry 3-1. James Maddison opened the scoring on his first start since May 2025, while Omar Marmoush netted his first goal for the club to restore their lead after Coventry had equalised. Ben Davies then wrapped it up with a stoppage-time third. The Blues have won their last six Premier League meetings with Tottenham, a run stretching back to November 2023. Spurs last won at Stamford Bridge in April 2018, their only league victory there since the competition began in 1992. Their most recent meeting ended 2-1 in favour of the West London side on 19 May 2026. Richarlison pulled one back for Spurs after the hosts had gone two goals ahead, but the defeat left their relegation battle unresolved until the final day of the season. A third successive league win would strengthen Chelsea’s position in the top four, while Spurs will be hoping to build on Monday’s result and climb further up the table. The match kicks off on Saturday, 24 October, at 17:30 BST.

item.title: Ballon d’Or Preview: Odds, prediction, and how to watch
item.description: (Photo by FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images) | FIFA via Getty Images For the first time in history, the prominent Ballon d’Or ceremony will be held in London. Besides a brief stint from 2010 to 2015 when the award was merged with FIFA’s World Player of the Year , it has traditionally been presented in various locations around Paris, France. Harry Kane is the heavy favorite, and a victory would break a few droughts. The last Bayern Munich winner was Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (1981). The last English winner was Michael Owen (2001). Furthermore, the last player to win the award who did not play for a French or Spanish club (or represent their national teams) was Manchester United’s Cristiano Ronaldo (2008). In addition to the coveted Ballon d’Or trophy, the presentation will also include the Kopa Trophy (best player under 21), Yashin Trophy (best goalkeeper), Gerd Müller Trophy (b est goalscorer), Coach of the Year, Club of the Year, and Sócrates Award (best humanitarian work). Streaming Info Location: London Palladium, London, United Kingdom Date: Monday, October 26th, 2026 Time: 6:00 PM local time (3:00 PM ET) TV/Streaming: Paramount Plus , CBS Sports Golazo Network, DAZN , Official Website SBN App: Engage with match threads on Bavarian Football Works from your phone with the new SB Nation app. Commenting and interacting with your communities is easier than ever with the Game Chat feature. The app is currently available in the U.S. on iOS and Android devices. Odds According to Polymarket , Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane has a 74% chance of winning the prestigious award. Over the summer, there was a lot of speculation that Kane might be out of the running because his teams lost in the semifinal stages of both the UEFA Champions League and the FIFA World Cup. However, thanks to general reason and a strong start to the 2026/27 seaso n, Kane is back in the pole position. Here are the resumes for each of the top contenders, spanning A ugust 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026: Harry Kane, Bayern Munich (74%): 73 goals, 8 assists, 5,207 minutes; Bundesliga champion and Golden Boot winner; DFB-Pokal champion and Golden Boot winner; Champions League semifinalist; World Cup third-place finish. Lamine Yamal, FC Barcelona (19%): 25 goals, 20 assists, 4,562 minutes; La Liga champion and assist leader; Champions League quarterfinalist; World Cup winner. Kylian Mbappé, Real Madrid (5%): 58 goals, 13 assists, 4,876 minutes; La Liga Golden Boot winner; Champions League quarterfinalist and Golden Boot winner; World Cup fourth-place finish and Golden Boot winner; set a new record with 22 career World Cup goals. Lionel Messi, Inter Miami (2%): 45 goals, 30 assists; MLS champion and Golden Boot winner; World Cup runner-up. There are a number of other players who will receive votes but do not have a realistic chance of winning: Michael Olise, Bayern Munich Ousmane Dembélé, PSG (2025 Ballon d’Or winner) Rodri, Manchester City (2024 Ballon d’Or winner) Erling Haaland, Manchester City Jude Belli

Kane had a historic season, scoring the most goals in Europe since Cristiano Ronaldo’s 2014/15 campaign. item.title: Red Bull tests new brakes in Austin to give Max Verstappen an edge
item.description: Red Bull Racing is testing new brake discs in Austin that are intended to give Max Verstappen more confidence under braking. GPblog understands that the modified Brembo discs should better suit the Dutchman's preferences. The main benefit should be a more predictable response from the brakes, both during an individual braking manoeuvre and over the course of a full race. After victories in Malaysia and Singapore, Red Bull is continuing to look for ways to improve the RB22. In Austin, this includes a modification to the front brakes. GPblog understands that the brake discs have a revised surface pattern. Red Bull hopes this will make their performance more consistent across a wider range of conditions. The initial response when Verstappen presses the brake pedal, also known as the ‘bite’, should remain roughly the same. The change is focused mainly on what happens after that. Why Red Bull are changing the brake discs When braking, the brake pads press against the rotating disc. The resulting friction slows the car and generates a great deal of heat. How predictably this process unfolds is important for the driver's confidence. The same pressure on the pedal should produce as similar and predictable a braking response as possible. Temperature plays an important role with carbon brakes. Brakes that are too cold or too hot can respond differently, forcing a driver to adjust their braking. In its technical explanation, Brembo therefore stresses the importance of a usable operating temperature range and a predictable response at different braking pressures. The modified surface pattern should help Red Bull improve that consistency. The exact appearance of the pattern and the physical mechanism that makes the difference are not known. The intended benefit, however, is clear: Verstappen should be able to rely on the same braking characteristics in a wider range of conditions. Max Verstappen hopes to benefit from this change by Red Bull Racing and Brembo - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool Max Verstappen hopes to benefit from this change by Red Bull Racing and Brembo - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool How Verstappen can benefit Braking involves more than simply pressing the pedal as hard as possible. As a driver approaches a corner, they initially brake hard, then gradually ease off the pressure. As they turn in, they may maintain some of that braking pressure. Precision is particularly important during this transition: the front tyres must both slow the car and steer it into the corner. A predictable response helps the driver coordinate those two tasks. If the brakes bite harder than expected, the risk of a wheel locking increases. If the braking effect is weaker than expected, the car may reach the corner carrying too much speed. This is where Verstappen could gain the most. If the braking remains more consistent as he eases off the pedal, he can judge more precisely how much speed to carry and how to position the car. GPblog understands that the brake discs have a revised surface pattern. Red Bull hopes this will make their performance more consistent across a wider range of conditions. The initial response when Verstappen presses the brake pedal, also known as the ‘bite’, should remain roughly the same. The change is focused mainly on what happens after that. Why Red Bull are changing the brake discs When braking, the brake pads press against the rotating disc. The resulting friction slows the car and generates a great deal of heat. How predictably this process unfolds is important for the driver's confidence. The same pressure on the pedal should produce as similar and predictable a braking response as possible. Temperature plays an important role with carbon brakes. Brakes that are too cold or too hot can respond differently, forcing a driver to adjust their braking. In its technical explanation, Brembo therefore stresses the importance of a usable operating temperature range and a predictable response at different braking pressures. The modified surface pattern should help Red Bull improve that consistency. The exact appearance of the pattern and the physical mechanism that makes the difference are not known. The intended benefit, however, is clear: Verstappen should be able to rely on the same braking characteristics in a wider range of conditions. Max Verstappen hopes to benefit from this change by Red Bull Racing and Brembo - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool Max Verstappen hopes to benefit from this change by Red Bull Racing and Brembo - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool How Verstappen can benefit Braking involves more than simply pressing the pedal as hard as possible. As a driver approaches a corner, they initially brake hard, then gradually ease off the pressure. As they turn in, they may maintain some of that braking pressure. Precision is particularly important during this transition: the front tyres must both slow the car and steer it into the corner. A predictable response helps the driver coordinate those two tasks. If the brakes bite harder than expected, the risk of a wheel locking increases. If the braking effect is weaker than expected, the car may reach the corner carrying too much speed. This is where Verstappen could gain the most. If the braking remains more consistent as he eases off the pedal, he can judge more precisely how much speed to carry and how to position the car. That could give him the confidence to brake closer to the limit of available grip. The change does not automatically mean Verstappen can brake later at every corner or immediately achieve a shorter stopping distance. Red Bull is primarily trying to make the brakes more predictable, so that he can repeat his preferred braking manoeuvre more often and more precisely. This could also prove valuable over a longer stint. Conditions change as a result of wear, fluctuating temperatures and a decreasing fuel load. Brakes that continue to respond reliably in those conditions require fewer adjustments from the driver. The test in Austin will show how much of an advantage the new discs actually deliver. The lessons learned can then also be applied to the development of the RB23 for 2027.

item.title: Serie A Preview: Lecce vs Juventus – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
item.description: Serie A Preview: Lecce vs Juventus – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Out-of-sorts Juventus head to Stadio Via del Mare desperately vying for a much-needed Serie A win against perennial strugglers Lecce. Anything other than three points in Puglia would significantly derail Luciano Spalletti’s chances of staying in the dugout beyond November’s international break. Confidence should be running high for Lecce after a thumping 3-0 victory at Udinese last weekend, which snapped their two-game losing league streak. More importantly, that win steered Eusebio Di Francesco’s side five points clear of the bottom three ahead of this round, relieving some pressure on the former Sassuolo and Roma boss. Lecce could now win back-to-back Serie A matches for the first time since the final two rounds of last season, a feat they managed just twice in the entire 2025/26 campaign. However, standing on the other side is a team eager to return to winning ways after a hugely disappointing week, highlighted by a dreadful 3-0 home defeat to Lazio. item.content:encoded: Serie A Preview: Lecce vs Juventus – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Out-of-sorts Juventus head to Stadio Via del Mare desperately vying for a much-needed Serie A win against perennial strugglers Lecce. Anything other than three points in Puglia would significantly derail Luciano Spalletti’s chances of staying in the dugout beyond November’s international break. Confidence should be running high for Lecce after a thumping 3-0 victory at Udinese last weekend, which snapped their two-game losing league streak. More importantly, that win steered Eusebio Di Francesco’s side five points clear of the bottom three ahead of this round, relieving some pressure on the former Sassuolo and Roma boss. Lecce could now win back-to-back Serie A matches for the first time since the final two rounds of last season, a feat they managed just twice in the entire 2025/26 campaign. Moreover, Lecce must punch above their weight here if they are to build on that triumph, a trait that has rarely been associated with Di Francesco’s side in recent years. For context, the hosts have picked up just one point from their last nine league clashes against teams starting the day in the top half. As if that’s not troubling enough, they have failed to get on the scoresheet in the last six such fixtures, offering very little hope that they could capitalize on Juventus’ rough patch. That said, they’ve only lost once on their last ten road trips (W5, D4), offering Spalletti some sort of comfort ahead of this must-win fixture. The record-time Italian champions have since gone unbeaten on six successive Serie A visits to the Via del Mare (W4, D2) despite scoring precisely one goal on five occasions in that stretch. Team News Lassana Coulibaly and Santiago Pierotti suffered injuries last week and will not be at Di Francesco’s disposal for this fixture. Francisco Conceicao, Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Jeff Ekhator, Kamil Grabara, and Manuel Locatelli are also unavailable, leaving Spalletti with several hard choices to make in what could prove a ‘make or break’ match for the veteran coach. Lecce vs Juventus Potential Starting Lineups Lecce (4-3-3): Falcone; Veiga, Gabriel, Gaspar, Gallo; Kaba, Ngom, Maleh; N’Dri, Geubbels, Monteiro. Juventus (3-4-1-2): Vicario; Kalulu, Bremer, Lucumi; McKennie, Luiz, Sarr, Cambiaso; Alajbegovic; Kolo Muani, Woltemade. Lecce vs Juventus Prediction It’s hard to expect this injury-hit Juventus side to stroll to three points in Puglia, but the visitors should have enough quality to get the job done. Lecce’s misfiring frontline could be their undoing against a superior opponent.

item.title: Game balls for SW Florida high school football top Week 10 performers
item.description: Cape Coral beat Charlotte to clinch its third consecutive district championship, Riverdale topped Immokalee, Estero won an offensive shootout over Aubrey Rogers and Naples continued its domination of county foes with a win over Barron Collier. Those were just some of the storylines from Week 10 of the 2026 high school football season in Southwest Florida. To honor the players who stood out, The News-Press and Naples Daily News hand out their Game Balls for the top efforts each week. Here are the honorees for this week's games. Ashton Alverio, Oasis Alverio passed for two touchdowns and rushed for another as the Sharks improved to 7-1 with a win over Gateway. Marquay Bradshaw, LaBelle The senior running back rushed for three touchdowns, including a 98-yard score, in the Cowboys' win over Bonita Springs. Paytrell Coleman, Ida Baker Coleman set school record with more than 400 rushing yards and five touchdowns in the Bulldogs' win over Palmetto Ridge. Noel Devine Jr., Cape Coral The freshman had a 65-yard rushing touchdown and a 28-yard receiving score in the Seahawks' win over Charlotte. Devin Dunford, Naples Dunford carried five times for 76 yards and three touchdowns in the Golden Eagles' win over Barron Collier. Bryson Ganley, ECS Ganley passed for five touchdowns, three to senior Mack Mitchell V, in the Sentinels' win over SFCA. Omarien Harris, Cape Coral The senior defensive end had two sacks and a forced fumble that teammate Carter Bernthaler returned for a touchdown in the Seahawks' district championship clinching win at Charlotte. Hudson King, Estero King caught 10 passes for 131 yards and three touchdowns in the Wildcats' win over Aubrey Rogers. Levi McKenzie, Riverdale The senior rushed for 153 yards and three touchdowns, caught a touchdown pass and also blocked a field goal in the Raiders' win at Immokalee. Liam Neary, Aubrey Rogers Neary rushed for 173 yards and a touchdown and also caught three passes for 56 yards and another score in the Patriots' loss to Estero. Maddox Stewart, Estero Stewart passed for 402 yards and five touchdowns and also ran for two scores in the Wildcats' victory over Aubrey Rogers. Daniel Volcy, Palmetto Ridge Volcy rushed 37 times for 409 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears' loss to Ida Baker. item.title: Preview: West Ham look to extend unbeaten run against promotion rivals Southampton
item.description: Preview: West Ham look to extend unbeaten run against promotion rivals Southampton Southampton travel to Stratford on Saturday to face an in-form West Ham side aiming for a 10-game unbeaten run. West Ham come into the game off an impressive 1-0 away win at league leaders, thanks to a first-half strike from Divine Mukasa. As for the Saints, they’re unbeaten in three after last weekend’s 0-0 draw against Bolton, where they were controversially denied a penalty after Leo Scienza’s cross seemingly hit Ruben Rodrigues’ arm. Going into the game, the visitors sit eighth on 17 points. However, if they hadn’t been deducted four points for breaching EFL rules at the beginning of the season, they would be in fourth. Meanwhile, West Ham’s result last Saturday puts them second in the table and makes them the highest-scoring side across England’s top four divisions, with 30 goals in their opening 11 Championship fixtures. These two sides have already met this season, in the second round of the Carabao Cup in late August. Southampton went into the game as favourites after West Ham’s poor start to the season. The Hammers fielded a very youthful side but pulled off a shock result, winning 4-1, with 19-year-old Josh Ajala scoring a brace on his full professional debut. The last league meeting was in April 2025 in the Premier League. Southampton’s Lesley Ugochukwu scored a 93rd-minute equaliser after Jarrod Bowen gave the Hammers the lead early in the second half. Ahead of the game, West Ham head coach Nuno Espírito Santo spoke to the press. “This week has been good, the boys have been working really hard, and we’re ready to compete. I’m glad we are scoring lots of goals, and if we continue and end up breaking records, it will be a fantastic thing for us, but we are focusing on competing and trying to get the right results. In terms of the number of goals, if we score more than our opponent, then we are happy.” The Hammers don’t have any new known injuries, with Keiber Lamadrid the only doubt after he missed the last few game weeks with a knee injury. Saints boss Tonda Eckert also spoke to the press on Friday, commenting on whether two key individuals will be involved in the capital. “Flynn [Downes] is getting better day after day; we’ll assess today, and he’s doing everything to be involved tomorrow. Cyle’s [Larin] injury was part of the hamstring towards the tendon, but it’s the same for him that he’s trying everything to make it tomorrow.” James Ward-Prowse is set to face West Ham for the first time since leaving the Hammers in the summer after spending three seasons with the club. A win for West Ham will extend their unbeaten league run to 10 games and add more pressure on Swansea. As for Southampton, a win will close the gap on the Hammers and push them closer to the summit of the table. The match is scheduled to kick off at 3pm BST on Saturday, October 24th.

item.title: Pastrana's big night leads Branson football over Logan-Rogersville
item.description: ROGERSVILLE — Vicente Pastrana’s cleats are anything but subtle. The cleats are jeweled, almost sparkling against the football turf. The black-and-red Nike cleats pop. Wearing this kind of shoe requires excellent play. In Branson’s biggest game of the season, Pastrana rose to the challenge. The quarterback accounted for all four touchdowns in Branson’s 28-21 win over Logan-Rogersville (8-1) on Friday, Oct. 23. High school football: Kicker Jonah Fields goes from afterthought to Missouri record book The win marked Branson’s third straight season as Ozark Mountain Conference champions. “I told our kids that it was going to be a battle. It came right down to it,” Branson head coach Aaron Hafner said. “I’m super proud of both sides of the ball figuring it out when they needed to, it was team football. That’s all you can ask for.” Branson (8-1) trailed 21-20 with 4:15 left in the game. Pastrana orchestrated a flawless closing drive. The run-first offense drove the length of the field, suffocating Rogersville’s defense. Pastrana led the Pirates on a 13-play, 80-yard drive. The senior scored the game-winning touchdown on a 1-yard rushing score. “It was nerve-wracking. All odds were against us, but we had to flip the switch, turn it on and get the yards. It was awesome,” Pastrana said. “Their defense is great, well-coached and disciplined.” Pastrana scored two other rushing touchdowns in the game. He also threw a 51-yard passing touchdown to Blake Weber on a swing pass in the first half. “He deserves everything that he gets,” Hafner said. “He’s a great leader and just an awesome human being. He’s a playmaker.” Nixa football: Inside the Eagles' fifth straight conference championship Trailing 20-7, Rogersville needed a spark and Joe Roche delivered. On a trick play, the running back launched a deep pass to Sky Vaughn. It set the Wildcats into the red zone and a few plays later, Roche scored a rushing touchdown. On the next possession, Pastrana fumbled a handoff, and Rogersville’s Lucas White recovered. Roche would peel off a 50-yard rushing touchdown, giving the Wildcats a 21-20 advantage. “The sweeps were getting shut down earlier, but I was going to run as hard as I possibly can,” Roche said. “I don’t really know how it happened. The next thing I know is that I jump cut and I was down the sidelines.” Pastrana’s fumble fell heavy on the senior. He explained that he didn’t want to let his team down in the final moments. That’s why he took it upon himself to deliver on the final drive. “I was really discouraged, for sure,” Pastrana said. “We always have to rise above it and overcome it. item.title: Does Notre Dame play today? Schedule, time, channel for next Irish football game
item.description: Does Notre Dame play today? Schedule, time, channel for next Irish football game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a strong 6-0 start, Notre Dame took its first hit against BYU last weekend. Now on a bye, the Fighting Irish will have extra time to recover and practice. Last week's primetime matchup against the Cougars had major implications for Notre Dame's title aspirations, especially given the program's playoff controversies in recent years. Though it's not over for the Fighting Irish, the team's national ranking did take a hit — they are now sitting in the No. 4 slot. Luckily, the Fighting Irish do not have a game scheduled for Week 8. Marcus Freeman and his team will be sure to utilize this bye to rest, recover and improve for the back half of their schedule. Notre Dame will face a spooky matchup upon return, going head-to-head with Navy on Halloween. Here's everything you need to know about Notre Dame's next game, including TV channel and streaming options for the Fighting Irish. When is Notre Dame's next game? item.title: 10 Takeaways: Nazem Kadri Delivers on His Promise Against Tampa Bay (+)
item.description: Mar 30, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Colorado Avalanche center Nazem Kadri (91) celebrates his first goal of the first period against the Calgary Flames at Ball Arena. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Nazem Kadri broke through with his first goal of the season on his 28th shot in his 11th game. If you had spoken to him throughout this goal-scoring drought, you would’ve never thought he had been dealing with it. Kadri is one of the more confident players on the roster and is very comfortable in his skin as that guy. I chatted with him before the Avs departed for the road trip, and again at practice on Thursday. Both times, he confidently said he’d break out of the scoring drought soon. He wasn’t worried about it. On Friday, before the game, he told me he’d score against Tampa Bay — a team he famously scored the biggest goal of his career against. He delivered. Also Read: Postgame: Six Different Goal Scorers Propel Avalanche to 6-3 Win Over Lightning 10 Takeaways 1. Having Kadri get one on the power play was as big as having him score in general. The top unit has been working hard to get over their own struggles, and Jared Bednar credited them for having an outstanding performance against the Lightning. They only ended up with three opportunities and the one goal, but they moved the puck well and seemed like they had more confidence in their decision-making. We’ll see if they can build on that on Sunday. 2. Going back to Kadri, he only had 16 goals last season, which is not up to par for his standards. He’s obviously not playing as big a role now as he was in Calgary, but I’d imagine he wants to be closer to the 25-35 goal mark like he was in the years before. He has 73 more games to build on tonight’s tally. Hopefully, for his sake, with a lot fewer shots ringing off the post. 3. Kadri entered the game with 27 shots, which was the second most among players with zero goals, behind Darren Raddysh’s 29. Zach Werenski and Dylan Cozens (25 shots each) round out the top three now that Kadri’s got one. 4. His power-play tally was, of course, set up by T.J. Hughes . I loved this response from Bednar postgame about Hughes’ ability to learn on the go. “I met with that line this morning. Actually, went through three games with them, and there were five or six points in that video session that I repeated. And like, first period alone, I noticed four or five of those six things that he immediately did better, so that takes an intelligent player. “The whole line, but especially T.J. His first period was phenomenal, right? And then we lose him for a bit in the second because we’re killing penalties the whole time, and he’s not doing that for us. And then he jumps back out and has the confidence. But I think he’s starting to skate a little more. The patience and his puck plays, it was phenomenal tonight. “But to be able to just take the information in the morning meeting and then implement it in the game just tells me how much growth we can still get out
item.content:encoded: Mar 30, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Colorado Avalanche center Nazem Kadri (91) celebrates his first goal of the first period against the Calgary Flames at Ball Arena. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Nazem Kadri broke through with his first goal of the season on his 28th shot in his 11th game. If you had spoken to him throughout this goal-scoring drought, you would’ve never thought he had been dealing with it. Kadri is one of the more confident players on the roster and is very comfortable in his skin as that guy. I chatted with him before the Avs departed for the road trip, and again at practice on Thursday. Both times, he confidently said he’d break out of the scoring drought soon. He wasn’t worried about it. On Friday, before the game, he told me he’d score against Tampa Bay — a team he famously scored the biggest goal of his career against. He delivered. Also Read: Postgame: Six Different Goal Scorers Propel Avalanche to 6-3 Win Over Lightning 10 Takeaways 1. Having Kadri get one on the power play was as big as having him score in general. The top unit has been working hard to get over their own struggles, and Jared Bednar credited them for having an outstanding performance against the Lightning.
