We’ll see if they can build on that on Sunday. 2. Going back to Kadri, he only had 16 goals last season, which is not up to par for his standards. He’s obviously not playing as big a role now as he was in Calgary, but I’d imagine he wants to be closer to the 25-35 goal mark like he was in the years before. He has 73 more games to build on tonight’s tally. Hopefully, for his sake, with a lot fewer shots ringing off the post. 3. Kadri entered the game with 27 shots, which was the second most among players with zero goals, behind Darren Raddysh’s 29. Zach Werenski and Dylan Cozens (25 shots each) round out the top three now that Kadri’s got one. 4. His power-play tally was, of course, set up by T.J. Hughes . I loved this response from Bednar postgame about Hughes’ ability to learn on the go. “I met with that line this morning. Actually, went through three games with them, and there were five or six points in that video session that I repeated. And like, first period alone, I noticed four or five of those six things that he immediately did better, so that takes an intelligent player. “The whole line, but especially T.J. His first period was phenomenal, right? And then we lose him for a bit in the second because we’re killing penalties the whole time, and he’s not doing that for us. And then he jumps back out and has the confidence. But I think he’s starting to skate a little more. The patience and his puck plays, it was phenomenal tonight. “But to be able to just take the information in the morning meeting and then implement it in the game just tells me how much growth we can still get out of T.J.” 5. Nathan MacKinnon became the third player to reach 20 points after the Edmonton Oilers duo of Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl. McDavid is already at 31 (hilarious, I know). Also, Artturi Lehkonen’s nine goals are tied for third in the NHL. He became the fourth player to reach nine goals after Kirill Kaprizov (11), Draisaitl (10) and Kyle Connor (nine). 6. Watching Andrei Vasilevskiy casually take a MacKinnon one-timer off the mask and continue play without skipping a beat was quite funny. He barely needed to readjust his helmet after the fact. I couldn’t believe it didn’t get damaged given how loud it sounded when the puck struck it. 7. Devon Toews had two goals in Calgary and added another tonight, which matches the three goals he had all of last season in just 11 games. 8. Toews’ 2025-26 season was uncharacteristically low for his standards, but it appears like that’s going to be a one-year blip. He has eight points in 11 games after recording 11 in 13 playoff games last spring. It’s safe to say he’s heading back toward his usual 50+ points. 9. Loved seeing Logan O’Connor back on the ice after the passing of his father two weeks ago. I can’t imagine how heavy his heart must feel during this difficult time. And he looked great. 10. I don’t know why the NHL has not yet made it mandatory for referees to always explain what they’re reviewing and what their determination is after the fact. I genuinely didn’t know what they were reviewing on that “challenge for a missed stoppage” play late in the second period. Like many, I thought it was because the puck may have gone out of play. But after looking back, you can see a replay where the Lightning player batted the puck down with a high stick and Brock Nelson was shouting to the officials that they had missed it mid-play. Regardless, the lack of a proper explanation from the referees, especially after a review that stretches for that long, is not a good look. Related Headlines 10 Takeaways: Avalanche Look Nothing Like Themselves After Back-to-Back Losses 10 Takeaways: Bednar’s Belief and Patience in T.J. Hughes Pays Off (+) 10 Takeaways: The Power Play Is Struggling and a New Voice Could Be on the Way (+) Read more at Colorado Hockey Now

item.title: Connor Hellebuyck Trade Return Underwhelming for Jets
item.description: Team USA goaltender Connor Hellebuyck. Getty The return the Winnipeg Jets got in the Connor Hellebuyck trade has to be as underwhelming as it gets. The Jets were long-rumored to want a king’s ransom for their former franchise goaltender. And even though Winnipeg got a boatload for Hellebuyck, the bottom line is that the return was largely underwhelming. Let’s start with Dawson Mercer. One of the requirements for Winnipeg was a top-six center. Well, Mercer isn’t quite that. The 24-year-old was the 18th overall pick in 2020. The Devils hoped he could become a solid second-line center, potentially moving Jack Hughes to the wing, and giving the club a solid playmaker behind Nico Hischier. Mercer had a great second season, scoring 27 goals and 56 points. He looked every bit the part, but hasn’t been able to replicate that same success. While he’s topped 20 goals twice in his career, he’s been playing bottom-six minutes. This season, Mercer has no goals and four points in 10 games. A change of scenery has been widely discussed, and, well, the Jets are hoping that will help the still-rising star find his potential. There’s another piece to consider in the Connor Hellebuyck trade: Nico Daws. At one point, the Devils hoped that Daws could become their number-one goalie. But he never quite got there. He’s put up decent numbers, but hadn’t really gotten the chance to play, as Jacob Markstrom and Jake Allen blocked his path. Daws has played all of 13 games in the last three seasons. And he’s someone the Jets hope can step in and become a solid tandem partner for Stuart Skinner. If his play this season is any indication, Daws may just work out after all. Jets Took on a Cap Dump in Connor Hellebuyck Trade One move that was evident in the Connor Hellebuyck trade was the cap dump that was Nick Bjugstad. The veteran forward, who’s currently on IR, was a necessary move to make the math work. Bjugstad has a $1.75 million cap hit, and, well, doesn’t really project to do much in Winnipeg. When he’s ready to return to play, Bjugstad could give the Jets some punch on the fourth line, while potentially chipping in some depth scoring. Winnipeg Also Got Some Magic Beans in the Deal What seems to be the most perplexing matter is the fact that the Jets did not get a first-round pick in the Connor Hellebuyck trade. In fact, one has to think that the Jets should have gotten multiple first-rounders out of it. Instead, the club got a second and seventh-rounder out of the deal. That’s something that Jets fans may question moving forward. GM Kevin Cheveldayoff should have pushed for at least one first-rounder. But then again, he might have been content with coming away with six total pieces in the deal. Lastly, there’s prospect Alexander Command. Since he was a first-round pick in this year’s draft, let’s assume he was the first-round pick the Jets would have wanted. There is no telling how much the 18-year-old will amount to. And so, he’s one of three magic beans the Jets got ou

item.title: Maple Leafs Legend Praises Mats Sundin for His Major Commitment to Toronto
item.description: TORONTO, ONTARIO - MAY 4: Mats Sundin speaks at a press conference where he was announced as Senior Executive Advisor of Hockey Operations and John Chayka was introduced as General Manager of the Toronto Maple Leafs at Real Sports Bar & Grill on May 4, 2026 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Michael Chisholm/Getty Images) Getty TORONTO, ON - NOVEMBER 17: Hall of Fame members (l-r) Doug Gilmour and Mats Sundin walk the red carpet prior to the induction ceremony at the Hockey Hall of Fame on November 17, 2014 in Toronto, Canada. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) Getty Maple Leafs legend Doug Gilmour shared his thoughts on Mats Sundin‘s executive role with the organization. Gilmour praised his former teammate for his commitment and decision to relocate to Toronto. Sundin returned to the organization last May after a disappointing season led MLSE to overhaul the Maple Leafs’ management and roster. The former Leafs captain was living in Sweden at the time. However, he decided to relocate his family and move back to Toronto so he could contribute full-time. Gilmour admitted that he was surprised that Sundin decided to get back into hockey, particularly in an executive role. He drew parallels between Sundin’s playing career and his current role. Doug Gilmour Shares His Thoughts on Mats Sundin’s Executive Role With the Maple Leafs Getty TORONTO, ON – NOVEMBER 17: Hall of Fame members (l-r) Doug Gilmour and Mats Sundin walk the red carpet prior to the induction ceremony at the Hockey Hall of Fame on November 17, 2014 in Toronto, Canada. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) While Doug Gilmour was surprised to see Mats Sundin return to hockey, he is happy to see Sundin involved with the Maple Leafs organization. Gilmour complimented his former teammate for his desire to win with the Maple Leafs. “I had no idea [that Sundin was getting back into hockey]. And to see it into effect, and him leaving Sweden to come back here and putting his heart and soul back into the game, just how he played. Yeah, I’m glad he did,” Gilmour told Unsportsmanlike Content . Gilmour believes that the same character traits would serve Sundin well in his new position. Sundin’s work ethic and experience can be helpful, as he can relate to the current Leafs roster. Gilmour Reflects on Playing With Sundin Gilmour also reflected on his time playing with Sundin on the Leafs. Sundin was acquired in a blockbuster trade that sent beloved captain Wendel Clark to the Quebec Nordiques. They spent two-and-a-half seasons as teammates but did not achieve playoff success. Gilmour recalled his time playing with Sundin and revealed that he was always focused on getting the best out of himself. “[Sundin] was very focused, obviously, going into the games. More importantly, on his days off and stuff, he really rehabbed himself and worked at his game, and he kind of stayed by himself. Sometimes, that’s how I was. You want to focus, you want downtime. And again, they say, don’t take the game hom

(Photo by Michael Chisholm/Getty Images) Getty TORONTO, ON - NOVEMBER 17: Hall of Fame members (l-r) Doug Gilmour and Mats Sundin walk the red carpet prior to the induction ceremony at the Hockey Hall of Fame on November 17, 2014 in Toronto, Canada. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) Getty Maple Leafs legend Doug Gilmour shared his thoughts on Mats Sundin‘s executive role with the organization. Gilmour praised his former teammate for his commitment and decision to relocate to Toronto. Sundin returned to the organization last May after a disappointing season led MLSE to overhaul the Maple Leafs’ management and roster. The former Leafs captain was living in Sweden at the time. However, he decided to relocate his family and move back to Toronto so he could contribute full-time. Gilmour admitted that he was surprised that Sundin decided to get back into hockey, particularly in an executive role. He drew parallels between Sundin’s playing career and his current role. Doug Gilmour Shares His Thoughts on Mats Sundin’s Executive Role With the Maple Leafs Getty TORONTO, ON – NOVEMBER 17: Hall of Fame members (l-r) Doug Gilmour and Mats Sundin walk the red carpet prior to the induction ceremony at the Hockey Hall of Fame on November 17, 2014 in Toronto, Canada. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) While Doug Gilmour was surprised to see Mats Sundin return to hockey, he is happy to see Sundin involved with the Maple Leafs organization. Gilmour complimented his former teammate for his desire to win with the Maple Leafs. “I had no idea [that Sundin was getting back into hockey]. And to see it into effect, and him leaving Sweden to come back here and putting his heart and soul back into the game, just how he played. Yeah, I’m glad he did,” Gilmour told Unsportsmanlike Content . Gilmour believes that the same character traits would serve Sundin well in his new position. Sundin’s work ethic and experience can be helpful, as he can relate to the current Leafs roster. Gilmour Reflects on Playing With Sundin Gilmour also reflected on his time playing with Sundin on the Leafs. Sundin was acquired in a blockbuster trade that sent beloved captain Wendel Clark to the Quebec Nordiques. They spent two-and-a-half seasons as teammates but did not achieve playoff success. Gilmour recalled his time playing with Sundin and revealed that he was always focused on getting the best out of himself. “[Sundin] was very focused, obviously, going into the games. More importantly, on his days off and stuff, he really rehabbed himself and worked at his game, and he kind of stayed by himself. Sometimes, that’s how I was. You want to focus, you want downtime. And again, they say, don’t take the game home with you. Take the game home with you, and that’s what happens,” Gilmour said. Gilmour and Sundin were reunited as teammates in 2003. However, Gilmour suffered a season-ending injury in his first game back, which led to his eventual retirement. Despite being teammates for only a short period, Gilmour has fond memories of playing with Sundin. In fact, Gilmour achieved a career milestone while playing with Sundin. “Mats was a great leader. My 1,000th point, he scored. And again, great memories. When he came in, I took care of him, and just the skill and the knowledge, that’s all you need.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Maple Leafs Legend Praises Mats Sundin for His Major Commitment to Toronto appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Alex Thornton's 4 TDs helps Jensen Beach bring home another district title
item.description: JENSEN BEACH — Regardless of Friday’s result, the Jensen Beach High School football team was in a good position to lift another trophy. If the Falcons lost, they would have been in a three-way tie with Fort Pierce Westwood and Heritage atop the District 13-4A standings and would have had to rely on their ranking at season’s end to be crowned district champions. Instead, Jensen Beach made sure there would be no reason to wait. The Falcons took care of business and left no doubt. Behind an outstanding rushing performance from Alex Thornton , Jensen Beach defeated Westwood 42-21 to outright claim the District 13-4A title Friday night at Jensen Beach High School. It is the program’s fourth district championship in the past five years and fifth overall, all under head coach Tim Caffey. “The kids set out a goal to be district champions, and they accomplished it tonight,” Caffey said. Watch the best high school football games in Florida Thornton spearheaded the Falcons’ championship push, finishing with touchdown runs of 2, 39, 20 and 7 yards. It marked the first four-touchdown game of his career. “I’m a dog. That’s what I’m supposed to do: make plays and win the game to help my team out,” Thornton said. Playing running back on offense and linebacker on defense, the senior was the best player on the field. He was especially dominant after halftime, scoring three of his four touchdowns in the second half. With Jensen Beach (7-2, 5-0 district) leading 14-7 and receiving the second-half kickoff, Thornton needed just two plays to extend the advantage. He followed a 22-yard run with a 39-yard touchdown sprint. He scored again later in the third quarter when he bounced outside and outran the defense on a 20-yard touchdown run. Thornton completed his barrage with his toughest run of the night. He barreled through multiple defenders and carried the pile into the end zone on a 7-yard touchdown run early in the fourth quarter. The senior also helped set up Jensen Beach’s first passing touchdown when he broke free for a 65-yard run down the sideline. That led to an 11-yard touchdown pass from Dre Lott to Tyrie McFadden early in the second quarter, giving the Falcons a 14-7 lead. Thornton finished with 15 carries for 215 yards. “Normally, we try to give him a break because he plays offense and defense. item.title: Hand football team rises up for SCC road win versus Shelton, stays undefeated
item.description: Tom Pshybyshefski caught a touchdown and threw for another TD to help Hand defeat Shnelton 35-12 at Finn Stadium Friday, Oct. 23, 2026. (Joe Morelli / Hearst Connecticut Media) SHELTON - Winning a football game on the road is never easy, especially in a league like the SCC that historically has several teams fighting for CIAC playoff berths. Hand picked up a quality win Friday night at Shelton, winning 35-12 at Finn Stadium. A quick start and a solid finish helped make up for a shaky middle portion of the game. "This is a huge one. Our team played amazing, battled the whole game, a great two weeks of practice leading up to this game," sophomore Tom Pshybyshefski said. Hand, ranked fourth in the GametimeCT Top 10 poll, moves to 6-0. "Any win over Shelton is a huge win," Hand football coach Erik Becker said. "... That's a phenomenal program, he's (Shelton coach Mike DeFelice) a great coach. That's a great team, they're always tough, they're well-coached. I can see them being a playoff team easily." Shelton (4-2) is one of those SCC teams in the fight for December games in Class L. The Gaels fell behind 21-0, but was able to score right before halftime and then in the third quarter to climb within 21-12. Cole St. Pierre (game-high 102 rushing yards, two touchdowns, two interceptions) scored on a 1-yard touchdown with 6 seconds left before halftime. The play was set up by a 39-yard reception by Evan Bouteiller down to the 1. St. Pierre's interception helped set up the possession. "We just saw something our receiver saying felt he could get by that kid and he did. "He made a great catch and a great throw by our quarterback," DeFelice said. "I told them I'd go to battle with them against anybody because we fought." Then the Gaels scored on their first possession of the second half. But that was all they were going to get. Lucca Boyce (92 yards, 16 carries) scored on a 3-yard touchdown run early in the fourth quarter to put Hand in control up 27-12. Boyce jumped to third all-time in program history with 2,655 yards, passing three players. Pshybyshefski, a receiver who caught a touchdown pass in the first half, threw for one in the fourth quarter, hitting a wide-open Tom Cahill (seven catches, 85 yards, two touchdowns) for the 22-yard touchdown. Pshybyshefski put the Tigers in good position with a 35-yard return off an interception. "Just a fade there, hit him, he's open. Great play call," Pshybyshefski said. Nate Kessell had a 5-yard return in the first half off a bad snap on a Shelton punt for Hand's second touchdown. Andrew King added a fumble recovery. Player of the Game Tom Pshybyshefski, Hand: Receiver caught a touchdown pass for Hand's third touchdown and threw a 22-yard touchdown pass to Thomas Cahill in the fourth quarter. Pshybyshefski also returned an interception 35 yards. Quotable "There's a lot of rivalries within the SCC. Everybody always asks, who's your rival? Who's your rival? I think in the SCC, it's week in and week out who your rival

item.title: Jayson Tatum defuses supposed beef with former teammate Jaylen Brown
item.description: BOSTON — When the lights were brightest on Friday night, Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum arguably had his best game since returning from an Achilles rupture in March. The six-time All-Star diced up the reigning champion New York Knicks at TD Garden, recording a game-high 36 points to go along with 9 rebounds and 7 assists during a thrilling 107-103 win. However, instead of fielding questions solely about his stellar performance, Tatum had to address the emoji heard 'round the world. On Thursday night, Tatum posted the third episode of his "Summer of Jayson" video series to YouTube. It featured a clip of him discussing the moment he learned former Celtics star Jaylen Brown had been traded to the rival Philadelphia 76ers. Tatum mentioned that he was shocked by the move, but Brown seemed to think otherwise, replying to the clip on Instagram with a baseball cap emoji — calling the statement "cap," or a lie. There was no further comment from Tatum's ex-partner in crime, yet the single emoji was enough to set Twitter ablaze and reignite talk of their being beef between the pair of 2024 NBA champions. Did Tatum orchestrate Brown's departure from Boston? Do the perennial All-Stars hate each other? Who is to blame for this offseason breakup? Tatum didn't have enough time at the podium on Friday to address every one of these narratives. But, he did spend almost 3 minutes responding to the emoji debacle when asked for his reaction. "I'm not much of an off-the-court entertainer type of guy, and for me, I don't have any animosity or beef or ill will towards him," Tatum began. "The frustrating part is since he's not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or the conversations haven't been enough about what we accomplished, all the games we won, winning the championship, how we've grown together. And it's turned into this drama type of thing." Jayson Tatum had a lengthy response to Jaylen Brown commenting a “cap” emoji under his video. They both belong in the top-10 of the Celtics' all-time scoring list and could have their jerseys hoisted to the rafters of TD Garden. So, to say their on-court partnership was fruitful might be an understatement. "Y'all kind of saw us grow up and everything that we accomplished, and I don't want that to be in the rearview mirror of what's being talked about," Tatum told the media. item.content:encoded: BOSTON — When the lights were brightest on Friday night, Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum arguably had his best game since returning from an Achilles rupture in March. The six-time All-Star diced up the reigning champion New York Knicks at TD Garden, recording a game-high 36 points to go along with 9 rebounds and 7 assists during a thrilling 107-103 win. However, instead of fielding questions solely about his stellar performance, Tatum had to address the emoji heard 'round the world. On Thursday night, Tatum posted the third episode of his "Summer of Jayson" video series to YouTube. It featured a clip of him discussing the moment he learned former Celtics star Jaylen Brown had been traded to the rival Philadelphia 76ers. Tatum mentioned that he was shocked by the move, but Brown seemed to think otherwise, replying to the clip on Instagram with a baseball cap emoji — calling the statement "cap," or a lie. There was no further comment from Tatum's ex-partner in crime, yet the single emoji was enough to set Twitter ablaze and reignite talk of their being beef between the pair of 2024 NBA champions. Did Tatum orchestrate Brown's departure from Boston? Do the perennial All-Stars hate each other? Who is to blame for this offseason breakup? Tatum didn't have enough time at the podium on Friday to address every one of these narratives. But, he did spend almost 3 minutes responding to the emoji debacle when asked for his reaction. "I'm not much of an off-the-court entertainer type of guy, and for me, I don't have any animosity or beef or ill will towards him," Tatum began. "The frustrating part is since he's not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or the conversations haven't been enough about what we accomplished, all the games we won, winning the championship, how we've grown together. And it's turned into this drama type of thing." Jayson Tatum had a lengthy response to Jaylen Brown commenting a “cap” emoji under his video. I recommend watching the whole video: “The frustrating part is since he's not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or the conversations haven't been enough about what we accomplished,… pic.twitter.com/1hztCN5pJx — Daniel Donabedian (@danield1214) October 24, 2026 In the 9 years Tatum and Brown played together, they reached five Eastern Conference Finals, two NBA Finals, and even won a title in 2024. They both belong in the top-10 of the Celtics' all-time scoring list and could have their jerseys hoisted to the rafters of TD Garden. So, to say their on-court partnership was fruitful might be an understatement. "Y'all kind of saw us grow up and everything that we accomplished, and I don't want that to be in the rearview mirror of what's being talked about," Tatum told the media. "It should be celebrated, right? How many people played in this league and never went to the Finals? We went twice and won a championship. So, it should be more about that." Given the fact that Tatum and Brown are on rival teams now and have been involved (largely unwillingly) in rumors intent on dividing them for several years, it may be difficult to salvage their relationship in the near future. Yet, Tatum still hopes it can be done with a candid conversation. "I’ve always wanted the best for him and wished the best for him," Tatum said. "I've seen all these things about ‘get your popcorn ready when they play,’ it’s not a (expletive) boxing match...Again, there's no animosity. There's no beef...There's not enough communication, and I think a conversation would solve or put out a lot of fires." When or if that sit-down happens remains to be seen. The Celtics and Sixers face each other for the first time this regular season on Tuesday, Nov. 10, and Tatum doesn't want that highly-anticipated contest to be a grudge match. "This ain't no (expletive) Shaq and Kobe," Tatum said in reference to the infamous feud between Los Angeles Lakers stars Shaquille O'Neal and Kobe Bryant. "It's not about that. It should be more praise, and I understand that doesn't necessarily sell. Drama gets clicks and views, but...that's not my thing." Brown will likely be asked about Tatum's comments in the next 24 hours or so. He could answer with a cold shoulder or animosity, which Tatum would understand to some degree due to the shocking nature of the offseason trade. "I reached out to him the day he got traded," Tatum recalled. "I called him, I texted him, and I understand people process things differently." Or, like Tatum, Brown could take the high road and settle this confusing situation before they suit up against one another in Philly. After all, Tatum did sound willing to chat with him in private, away from mics and media narratives. I’ve already seen Jayson Tatum’s answer to Jaylen Brown’s IG comment get taken out of context. So here’s the entire transcript of the quote: pic.twitter.com/ki8pzNNYR3 — Daniel Donabedian (@danield1214) October 24, 2026 "There's a conversation to be had," Tatum stated. "We can definitely have that conversation. I welcome that." No matter what happens, Tatum will remain focused on improving the record of the 1-1 Celtics and, most importantly, taking care of his family. "I got two kids," Tatum said in an almost exasperated manner. "At this point in our lives, we’re too old to be having our relationship discussed, X, Y, and Z, on the Internet." item.title: Byrd, Haughton, Loyola, North DeSoto, Northwood among Friday winners
item.description: A spectacular night of North Louisiana football saw Byrd win its first game of the 2026 season, Haughton move to 8-0 for the first time in forever and North DeSoto needing 78 points to put away Franklin Parish. And then there was Green Oaks falling short of setting a school record 8-game win streak due to a domination by Homer and Loyola putting up big numbers despite the flu running rampant through the school. Byrd 28, Evangel 24: Senior Christian Maxie rushed 20 times for 210 yards, including a pair of 46-yarders in the fourth quarter, to give the Jackets (1-7) their first win of the season. The Eagles (4-4) were without LSU commit Peyton Houston (shoulder injury), but freshman Briggs Berlin completed 16 of 26 passes for 216 yards and two TDs. Loyola 50, Bastrop 16: Bryce Restovich completed 15 of 19 passes for 295 yards and 6 TDs as the Flyers (5-3) ran away from the Rams (4-4). Ty Walsworth and Charlie McKenzie had two TD receptions apiece. EVANGEL ACE: Evangel’s Aiden Carter is a Swiss Army Knife for the Eagles Haughton 42, Airline 21: Brandon Craig put up four rushing TDs and added a TD reception from Taylor Weathersby as the Bucs (8-0) are undefeated this late in the season for the first time since 2014. Haughton got an interception from Colton Bedgood and a fumble recovery by Isaac Jennings against Airline (6-2). Chase Williams tossed a pair of TD passes and ran for another for the Vikings. Dylan Johnson nailed all four PATs. Shaw 24, Calvary 7: Hudson Price hit Braylun Huglon for the only TD the Cavaliers (7-1) could muster against Shaw (7-1). North DeSoto 78, Franklin Parish 64: The game of the week in Louisiana saw the Griffins (8-0) remain undefeated thanks to 5 rushing TDs and 260 yards from Hayden Bell against the Patriots (5-3). Mason Smith was 25-for-32 for 320 yards and 3 TDs while Derik White rushed 24 times for 251 yards and 3 TDs. Braylon Moore caught 9 passes for 121 yards and a score. East Ascension 48, Parkway 32: The Panthers (4-4) saw Bryston McCoy complete 26 of 45 passes for 355 yards and a score, while Damian Dacaldacal rushed 24 times for 170 yards and 3 TDs, but it wasn’t enough against EA (7-1). Gary Burney had 10 receptions for 137 yards and Tristan Sedberry had 7 for 99 yards. Northwood 44, Bossier 14: The Falcons (4-4) stayed on a winning roll behind two TDs apiece from Dez Douglas and Caden Stewart. Bossier (3-5) saw Jaylon James toss TD passes to Jaylon Bacon and Dmarea Bates. Cedar Creek 62, Arcadia 6: The Cougars (8-0) remained undefeated thanks to four TDs and 208 rushing yards from Payton Harris. Brett Bell scored twice against the Hornets (0-8). Minden 52, Southwood 13: The Tide (6-2) got three TDs from Abreon Curry, including one on a 67-yard kickoff return, to slide past the Cowboys (1-7). Lucas Owens rushed 16 times for 176 yards and two scores. Haynesville 53, Lincoln Prep 0: Donnie and Moise Critton combined for 170 rushing yards and three TDs as the Tors (6-1) rolled past the Panthers (3-5). St. Mary

Northwood 44, Bossier 14: The Falcons (4-4) stayed on a winning roll behind two TDs apiece from Dez Douglas and Caden Stewart. Bossier (3-5) saw Jaylon James toss TD passes to Jaylon Bacon and Dmarea Bates. Cedar Creek 62, Arcadia 6: The Cougars (8-0) remained undefeated thanks to four TDs and 208 rushing yards from Payton Harris. Brett Bell scored twice against the Hornets (0-8). Minden 52, Southwood 13: The Tide (6-2) got three TDs from Abreon Curry, including one on a 67-yard kickoff return, to slide past the Cowboys (1-7). Lucas Owens rushed 16 times for 176 yards and two scores. Haynesville 53, Lincoln Prep 0: Donnie and Moise Critton combined for 170 rushing yards and three TDs as the Tors (6-1) rolled past the Panthers (3-5). St. Mary’s 58, Lakeview 6: The Tigers (7-1) got three rushing TDs from John Paul Thibodaux and two passing TDs from Preston Tilley in blasting past the Gators (2-6). Jayd Linebaugh returned a fumble for a score and Dennison Morgan added a rushing TD. item.title: Grace Egan returns briefly for Wisconsin volleyball. Is she truly back?
item.description: MADISON – Grace Egan is back. Well, sort of. The Wisconsin outside hitter subbed in during the fourth set of the sixth-ranked Badgers ’ Oct. 23 loss to No. 21 Washington. Her first time on the court since missing several weeks with a back injury came in a very limited capacity, though. She came in ahead of the last point of the fourth set to serve, with the Badgers trailing, 24-18. After Washington eventually won the point and the set, Egan remained on the sideline for the entire fifth set. "She told me yesterday she's back, and I said, 'OK, alright, you're back,'" Wisconsin coach Kelly Sheffield said. "But she hasn't done much practices. So just because she says she's back doesn't mean that, alright, here, let's just get you out on the court." Egan's entrance came with a loud ovation from the UW Field House crowd – officially listed at 7,229 although actual turnout was obviously lower. That resounding reaction was part of Sheffield's calculus for giving Egan the limited opportunity against the Huskies. "I figured, alright, it's getting late; people are grumpy," Sheffield said with a quick aside to ask for the World Series score. "We were getting popped at that point, and I was hoping to get the crowd into it a little bit. And they did." Big ovation from the UW Field House crowd as #Badgers outside hitter Grace Egan subs in to serve. First match for her since Sept. 2 after dealing with a back injury. pic.twitter.com/W0brsyn7hi — John Steppe (@JSteppe1) October 24, 2026 While Egan's first opportunity in the front row will have to wait for another time, simply being on the court in any capacity is a milestone in her recovery. Egan shared in a Sept. 14 Instagram post that the injury “brought a level of fear and stress I hadn’t experienced before.” She ended up missing 13 matches, with UW going 11-2 during that stretch. Both losses were against ranked teams. Before her injury, Egan totaled 37 kills in four matches while hitting .242. That included a 17-kill performance in UW's narrow five-set win over Florida. Her nine service aces were tied for fourth on the Badgers heading into the Washington match despite her extended absence. Egan not-so-subtly hinted at the Oct. 23 return on social media, posting a video on Instagram on Oct. 22 with “I’M BACK” text appearing on top of footage of her running from the locker room to the court. This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Grace Egan returns briefly for Wisconsin volleyball. Is she truly back?

item.title: Dana White Praises Alexander Volkanovski Before UFC 333
item.description: Alexander Volkanovski UFC 333 Dana White Getty UFC president Dana White praised UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski ahead of his title fight at UFC 333. Volkanovski puts his belt on the line against undefeated Russian Movsar Evloev in the main event of UFC 333. Ahead of the bout, White praises Volkanovski for everything he has accomplished during his UFC Hall of Fame career. Dana White Praises Alexander Volkanovski Speaking to Main Event before UFC 333, White showered Volkanovski with high praise before he locks horns with Evloev. “He’s one of the greatest of all time, and he’s obviously become a huge star for us, too,” White said. Dana White Ranks Alexander Volkanovski’s Greatest UFC Moments As a two-time UFC featherweight champion who has fought and defeated many of the greatest featherweights in MMA history, Volkanovski certainly has had his fair share of legendary UFC moments. White, though, can point to a few fights in particular that have stood out to him during Volkanovski’s legendary UFC run. “There’s been a lot. The most recent was winning the title again (against Diego Lopes) at his age. The Max Holloway fights, there’s been so many things. The (Brian) Ortega fight, getting out of that choke. He’s made a huge impact on this company on this company, on that weight division, and obviously for Australian MMA,” White said. This Saturday at UFC 333 , Volkanovski fights Evloev in his latest title defense as he takes on an undefeated opponent whom many other featherweights don’t exactly want to fight given how much of a difficult fighting style he has with his elite grappling skills. Volkanovski, though, has made it clear that he wants to fight the best opponents possible, and he asked the UFC several times to fight Evloev before he was finally granted the opportunity to face him. It won’t be an easy fight for Volkanovski, who is basically at Pick ’em odds for his next title defense. But should he win this fight, it could catapult him to a potential superfight against UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje , a fellow 38-year-old legend of the sport whom Volkanovski had made it clear he is interested in fighting. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Dana White Praises Alexander Volkanovski Before UFC 333 appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Three Italian giants vying for Man Utd star amid contract uncertainty
item.description: Three Italian giants vying for Man Utd star amid contract uncertainty Manchester United full-back Diogo Dalot is being linked with a potential return to Italy, especially if he doesn’t renew his contract in the coming months. The 27-year-old is one of the club’s longest-serving players, having joined the Red Devils in the summer of 2018, completing a £20 million move from Porto. The Portuguese struggled for playing time in his early days at Old Trafford, so he was sent out on loan to AC Milan for the 2020/21 season. Dalot attracts interest from Juventus, Inter & Milan (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) After finding some success at San Siro, Dalot was happy to extend his spell with the Rossoneri. However, the two clubs couldn’t find an agreement, so the right-back returned to Carrington. Dalot then gradually cemented himself as a regular starter at Man Utd. He has been the club’s first choice on the right side since Erik ten Hag’s reign. But with his contract expiring in June 2028 and no signs of a renewal just yet, the player’s future is engulfed in uncertainty. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport journalist Fabiana Della Valle, Juventus, Inter, and Milan have all enquired about the Portuguese international. The pink newspaper believes that a return to Serie A could become a concrete possibility if MUFC don’t offer the player a new contract in the next few months. Milan could have the advantage due to his previous stint at the club. The Rossoneri would also give him the chance to reunite with Ruben Amorim, at least if the latter stays in his position next season. What should Man Utd do with Diogo Dalot? (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Like the rest of the Man Utd squad, Dalot has had some difficult moments over the past few weeks. The Braga native was particularly poor in the defeat to 10-man Manchester City before the international break. However, some stats suggest Dalot deserves more plaudits than he’s receiving . For instance, he created more chances (14) than any other defender in the Premier League this season. Ideally, United should upgrade their entire backline in 2027, including the right-back role. That being said, Dalot could be suited for a back-up role thanks to his growing importance in the locker room, his willingness to leave it all on the pitch, and his ability to play on either flank. item.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
item.description: Arteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’ Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue. Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks. Continue reading...

item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result. Continue reading...

item.title: NWSL drops controversial criteria around ‘Rodman Rule’ in settlement with NWSLPA
item.description: Any player will be eligible for High Impact Player status Requirements had included top 100, marketability lists Sides also resolve grievance on Rodman contract refusal The NWSL and the NWSL Players Association have reached a settlement to drop the restrictive criteria around the controversial High Impact Player (HIP) rule, allowing any player to earn the league’s highest salaries. The NWSL introduced the rule late last year, allowing teams to spend an additional $1m above the salary cap to sign star players. Players with the designation had to meet one of eight criteria, ranging from US national team minutes and Ballon d’Or recognition to NWSL Best XI honors to media lists, including the Guardian’s Top 100 and a ranking that ordered athletes by marketability. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
item.description: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA Continue reading...

item.title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby
item.description: Gunners’ title hopes have seemingly evaporated and their under-pressure head coach faces her latest test against Spurs on Saturday It says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 goals in two games are not the side whose head coach is under most pressure before a north London derby. Tottenham, four points above their neighbours before Saturday’s meeting, may have been humbled in consecutive Women’s Super League matches but all eyes are on Renée Slegers. Arsenal are winless in five WSL matches for the first time, and the most decorated club in English women’s football desperately need a turning point. Their failure to beat Birmingham at home last Saturday, dropping points against a promoted side for the second time this season, again demonstrated the team’s inability to convert possession into goals. They increasingly look like a team stuck in Groundhog Day. Continue reading...

Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.description: Funds for 2027 will match men’s World Cup in 2026 Players given better flights and individual hotel rooms Teams in the 2027’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil will receive the same preparation money from Fifa as those that played at the 2026 men’s tournament, the world’s governing body has announced. item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
